items.title: 67802_Charles Mingus oral history interview
items.q: There's a guy came to the club, wanted to see my man on tenor saxophone... I might have if I didn't have George Adams there at the same time.

ctx.x: That's right, well, I did all kinds of things for the station. The jazz shows I did for nothing, just to keep my sanity.
You were doing jazz when I first met you. You did -- George (inaudible).

items.title: 67802_Charles Mingus oral history interview
items.q: That's why I didn't mess with mention Bunny Bluett George Adams and Buddy Bluett, because they weren't playing my music.

ctx.x: I'm not saying they didn't steal from you. Everybody stole from you. I'm talking about getting the band to sound the way you did. Your bands always had so much fire and energy.

Yeah, because I had amateur musicians. I never used the guys who -- yes, I did, I had Ernie Henry Hiemann one time, I had one of the best. It was at a time he was playing good, too. I never had guys like Benny Bailey or Ernie Henry Hiemann at the same time in the band. Always got a sound ensemble that would play, but solos were never up to par with what the arrangements were.
